text:
julie.support: FYI customer (acme) opened a ticket — sudden p99 jump for tiny prompts (<=16 tokens) since ~02:30 UTC. Also seeing intermittent 401s for some requests. They included a curl repro and timing. Can someone triage?

maria.sre: putting on page. any quick logs or tenant-id?

julie.support: tenant acme-42. curl repro: `curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hi"}' -w '%{time_total}\n'` => usually 0.09s, now getting 1.6s p99 and occasional 502/401 spikes.

kevin.eng: 1.6s p99 for a 1-token prompt screams batching hold-window. any config changes rolled out last night?

maria.sre: checking deploys... there was a micro-config roll for continuous-batcher grace-window to 8ms for all tenants at 01:50 UTC (attempt to improve throughput).

ingrid.ml: that will hurt tiny prompts — longer hold increases tail. also if auth retries cause re-queuing, tiny requests can pile up.

sre-bot: alert: acme-42 p99 latency increased 17x at 02:28 UTC; batcher.grace_window set -> 8ms (from 2ms) on pool gpu-dedicated-2; sample requests queued=3 avg

kevin.eng: can we repro locally quickly by hammering small requests with the new grace? I'll run a short script.

kevin.eng: (after 2m) repro confirmed on staging: p99 ~1.5s when grace_window=8ms and small_request_coalesce enabled. When set to 2ms p99 goes to ~0.12s.

maria.sre: logs from the customer's node show lots of tiny batches of size 12 but with one long hold due to an auth retry:
```
2026-03-12T02:31:02Z INFO batcher: enqueued req tid=acme-42 rtt=0.011
2026-03-12T02:31:02Z WARN auth: token expired for req id=xyz, retrying
2026-03-12T02:31:02Z INFO batcher: hold-window start tid=acme-42 duration_ms=8
2026-03-12T02:31:02Z INFO batcher: flush batch size=12 elapsed_hold_ms=812
```
Note the elapsed_hold_ms=812 — something blocked the batch long after the nominal 8ms.

ingrid.ml: blocking could be due to retry backoff or synchronous KMS call for token refresh. acme uses KMS-backed token validation?

julie.support: customer confirms they rotated keys and had a transient KMS latency spike around 02:30 UTC. They say it recovered but p99 remained bad for ~10-15m.

kevin.eng: aha — combo of increased grace_window + occasional long auth validation caused some batches to wait on slow requests and produce long tail. Two-pronged mitigation: reduce grace_window for small-request tenants and enable bypass-hotpath for requests that have >1 retry.

maria.sre: propose immediate mitigations (quick, low-risk):
1) rollback grace_window for tenant acme-42 to 2ms (temp)
2) enable per-tenant small_request_mode=true (routes <=32 token requests to fast path, bypass coalescer)
3) add temporary traffic-split for acme-42 to older config (canary -> 0.0 -> backfill)
4) ask ops to check KMS latency / token pipeline and increase auth timeout to not block batcher threads

ops_tom: I can bump auth validation timeout and switch token validation to async for affected pool. Doing that now for gpu-dedicated-2.

kevin.eng: I'll push a hotpatch: set batcher.grace_window_acme-42=2ms and small_request_mode=true for the tenant via configstore. Command: `redctl config set /pools/gpu-dedicated-2/tenants/acme-42/batcher/grace_window_ms 2`

maria.sre: sounds good. Kevin, after hotpatch, can you watch p95/p99 for next 30m and then do a controlled canary of the 8ms change with traffic shift?

kevin.eng: hotpatch applied. immediate metrics: p99 dropped from 1.6s -> 0.11s for acme-42. auth 401 error rate also fell after async validation enabled.

julie.support: relayed to customer — they're pleased. they asked for longer-term fix suggestions.

ingrid.ml: long-term: implement per-tenant adaptive grace that shrinks for small prompt distributions; add circuit-breaker so a single slow request doesn't hold a batch beyond Xms (hard cap flush). Also track auth retry path latencies and surface in console per-tenant.

maria.sre: file follow-up ticket: SRE-6221 (implement adaptive grace + batch hard-flush for slow dependencies). Assign to eng-batcher and eng-auth.

julie.support: thanks all — closing escalation with customer note. :white_check_mark:

sre-bot: incident-note created: SRE-6221 linked to ticket #8712; postmortem optional if recurrence.
